prerak_kahani.title: The Golden Swan
prerak_kahani.story: A magical swan lived in a pond and occasionally shed a golden feather. A poor woman discovered this and started collecting the feathers to feed her family. She soon became greedy and decided to catch the swan and pluck all its feathers at once so she could be rich instantly. When she plucked the feathers, they instantly turned into ordinary, worthless white feathers. She lost her daily source of income.
prerak_kahani.moral: Greed destroys what you already have. Be patient and grateful for small blessings.

prerak_kahani.title: The Two Crabs
prerak_kahani.story: A mother crab and her baby were walking on the beach. The mother crab scolded her baby, saying, 'Why do you walk sideways like that? You should always walk straight forward with your toes pointed out.' The baby crab replied, 'Show me how to walk straight, Mother, and I will gladly follow your example.' The mother crab tried, but could only walk sideways herself.
prerak_kahani.moral: Example is the best precept. Do not expect others to follow rules that you cannot follow yourself.

prerak_kahani.title: The Wolf and the Crane
prerak_kahani.story: A wolf got a bone stuck in his throat and was choking. He begged a crane to put her long neck down his throat to pull it out, promising a handsome reward. The crane carefully removed the bone and then asked for her reward. The wolf grinned, bared his teeth, and said, 'Your reward is that you put your head in a wolf's mouth and took it out safely. Now go away.'
prerak_kahani.moral: Expect no reward for serving the wicked; escaping unharmed is reward enough.

prerak_kahani.title: The Eagle and the Arrow
prerak_kahani.story: A majestic eagle was soaring through the sky when he was suddenly pierced by a hunter's arrow. As he fell to the ground, he looked at the arrow that had fatally wounded him and noticed that the back of the arrow was guided by feathers from his own wings. He sighed with his last breath, realizing his own kind had helped create the weapon that destroyed him.
prerak_kahani.moral: We often unknowingly give our enemies the means for our own destruction.

word_of_the_day.meaning: The action of betraying one's country, a group, or a person; treachery.

prerak_kahani.title: The Lion, the Bear, and the Fox
prerak_kahani.story: A lion and a bear simultaneously caught a small deer. They fought fiercely over who would get to eat it. They fought for hours until both were completely exhausted, bruised, and unable to stand. A fox, who had been watching from behind a bush, casually walked over, grabbed the deer, and trotted away while the two mighty beasts lay helpless on the ground.
prerak_kahani.moral: When two people stubbornly fight over something, a third party often walks away with the prize.

word_of_the_day.meaning: A person who exploits circumstances to gain immediate advantage rather than being guided by consistent principles.

prerak_kahani.title: The Boys and the Frogs
prerak_kahani.story: A group of young boys were playing by a pond. They started throwing stones into the water, aiming at the frogs for fun, hitting and killing several of them. Finally, one brave frog popped its head out of the water and pleaded, 'Please stop! What is just a fun game to you is a matter of life and death to us.'
prerak_kahani.moral: One person's careless entertainment shouldn't become another's tragedy. Consider how your actions affect others.

word_of_the_day.meaning: Thoughtfulness and sensitivity towards others.
word_of_the_day.example: He showed great consideration for his tired colleagues by taking on the extra work.

prerak_kahani.title: The Boy and the Filberts
prerak_kahani.story: A young boy found a jar full of delicious filberts (hazelnuts). He reached his hand in and grabbed as many nuts as his fist could possibly hold. But when he tried to pull his hand out, the neck of the jar was too narrow for his oversized fist to pass through. Unwilling to drop a single nut, he sat there and cried. A passerby said, 'Drop half the nuts, and your hand will slide out easily.'
prerak_kahani.moral: Do not attempt too much at once. Greed will leave you stuck with nothing.

word_of_the_day.meaning: The avoidance of excess or extremes, especially in one's behavior or choices.
word_of_the_day.example: Eating sweets in moderation is fine, but eating too many will ruin your health.

prerak_kahani.title: The Fox and the Woodcutter
prerak_kahani.story: A fox being chased by hunters begged a woodcutter to hide him. The woodcutter let the fox hide in his hut. When the hunters arrived and asked if he had seen the fox, the woodcutter verbally said 'No,' but subtly pointed his finger toward the hut. The hunters didn't understand his gesture and ran off. The fox slipped out without thanking the man. When the woodcutter got angry, the fox replied, 'I would have thanked you if your hand had matched your words.'
prerak_kahani.moral: Your actions speak louder than your words. Do not act deceitfully.

word_of_the_day.meaning: The practice of claiming to have higher standards or more noble beliefs than is the case.
word_of_the_day.example: He criticized people for being late, yet he never showed up on time himself, showing pure hypocrisy.

prerak_kahani.title: The Camel and the Arab
prerak_kahani.story: An Arab was sleeping inside his warm tent on a freezing desert night. His camel outside asked, 'Master, it is freezing. May I just put my nose inside?' The master agreed. A while later, the camel asked to bring in its neck, then its front legs, and finally its whole body. The tent was too small for both of them, and the massive camel ended up pushing its master out into the cold night.
prerak_kahani.moral: Give a little space to an encroacher, and they will soon take over everything.

word_of_the_day.meaning: Intrusion on a person's territory, rights, or personal life.
word_of_the_day.example: The neighbors complained about the new fence, calling it an encroachment on their property line.

prerak_kahani.title: The Tortoise and the Eagle
prerak_kahani.story: A tortoise grew tired of crawling on the ground and wanted to fly. He begged an eagle to teach him. The eagle explained that tortoises do not have wings and are not built for the sky. The tortoise insisted stubbornly. Finally, the eagle picked him up, soared high into the clouds, and let go. The tortoise plummeted to the earth and shattered his shell on the rocks.
prerak_kahani.moral: Do not stubbornly strive for things completely outside your nature. Listen to the advice of those who know better.

word_of_the_day.meaning: Excessive pride or self-confidence.
word_of_the_day.example: The general's hubris led him to underestimate the enemy's strength, resulting in a crushing defeat.

prerak_kahani.title: The Farmer and the Viper
prerak_kahani.story: A farmer walking through his snowy fields found a viper completely frozen from the cold. Pitying the creature, the farmer picked it up and placed it inside his coat to warm it up. The warmth revived the snake. Instinctively, the viper bit its benefactor, delivering a fatal dose of venom. As the farmer fell dying, he realized he had trusted a creature whose nature was strictly to harm.
prerak_kahani.moral: The greatest kindness will not change the nature of the ungrateful and malicious.

word_of_the_day.meaning: An ungrateful person.

prerak_kahani.title: The Ass in the Lion's Skin
prerak_kahani.story: An ass found a lion's skin left by a hunter. He dressed himself in it and walked toward his village, terrifying all the people and animals along the way. Feeling very proud of himself, he tried to roar like a mighty lion to scare them even more. But instead of a roar, a loud, ridiculous bray came out. The villagers instantly realized it was just an ass, pulled the skin off him, and chased him away.
prerak_kahani.moral: Fine clothes may disguise a fool, but silly words will always disclose their true nature.

word_of_the_day.meaning: A claim or the assertion of a claim to something; the use of affectation to impress.
word_of_the_day.example: He spoke with great pretension, using large words he didn't fully understand to seem smarter.

prerak_kahani.title: The Eagle and the Jackdaw
prerak_kahani.story: An eagle swooped down from a cliff, snatched a small lamb in its powerful talons, and carried it away. A small jackdaw watched this and thought, 'I can do that too!' He flew down and tried to grab a massive, heavy ram. Instead of lifting it, his claws got hopelessly tangled in the thick fleece. The shepherd saw him flapping helplessly, caught him, clipped his wings, and gave him to his children as a pet.
prerak_kahani.moral: Do not let vanity make you overestimate your powers. Know your limitations.

prerak_kahani.title: The Mouse, the Frog, and the Hawk
prerak_kahani.story: A mouse and a frog were friends. As a practical joke, the frog tied the mouse's leg to his own. Later, they reached a pond. The frog jumped in, diving deep, and forgot about the mouse. The mouse drowned and floated to the surface. A hawk flying above saw the mouse, swooped down, and grabbed it. Because the frog was tied to the mouse, the hawk ended up getting two meals for the price of one.
prerak_kahani.moral: Harm set, harm get. If you create a trap or plan poorly for others, you will likely fall into it yourself.

word_of_the_day.meaning: The intention or desire to do evil; ill will.
word_of_the_day.example: She acted without any malice, merely making a clumsy mistake rather than trying to cause trouble.

prerak_kahani.title: The Two Pots
prerak_kahani.story: A heavy brass pot and a fragile earthen pot were sitting on a riverbank when a flash flood swept them both into the raging water. The brass pot called out, 'Stay close to me, my friend! I will protect you from the rocks.' The earthen pot replied, 'That is exactly what I am afraid of! If I hit the rocks, I break. But if the current slams you into me, I will shatter into pieces just the same. It is safer if we stay apart.'
prerak_kahani.moral: Equals make the best friends. Be cautious when associating with those who are much stronger and can easily crush you, even unintentionally.

prerak_kahani.title: The Ant and the Chrysalis
prerak_kahani.story: An ant was running around looking for food when he saw a chrysalis (a pupa of a butterfly) lying on the ground. The ant mocked the poor creature, saying, 'What a sad existence you have! You are trapped in that shell, while I can run freely wherever I want.' The chrysalis heard but said nothing. A few days later, the ant passed by the same spot and saw a magnificent butterfly emerging from the broken shell. The butterfly spread its colorful wings and flew into the sky, leaving the amazed ant far below.
prerak_kahani.moral: Appearances can be deceiving. Everyone has their own time to grow and bloom.

word_of_the_day.meaning: A thorough or dramatic change in form or appearance.
word_of_the_day.example: The caterpillar's transformation into a butterfly is one of nature's greatest wonders.

prerak_kahani.title: The Frog and the Ox
prerak_kahani.story: A small frog saw a massive ox grazing in a meadow and was filled with envy at the ox's grand size. The frog decided he wanted to be just as big. He took a deep breath and puffed himself up. He asked his friends, 'Am I as big as the ox yet?' They said no. He puffed up even more, but they still said no. Determined to be the biggest, the frog puffed and puffed with all his might until, suddenly, he burst.
prerak_kahani.moral: Do not pretend to be something you are not. Pride and envy will only lead to your destruction.

word_of_the_day.meaning: A feeling of discontented or resentful longing aroused by someone else's possessions, qualities, or luck.
word_of_the_day.example: He watched with envy as his colleague received the award.

did_you_know.fact: Did you know? The blood of a lobster is entirely colorless until it is exposed to oxygen, at which point it turns blue.

prerak_kahani.title: The Cat and the Mice
prerak_kahani.story: A very skilled cat had caught so many mice in a house that the remaining mice were terrified to leave their holes. Knowing they were hiding, the cat decided to trick them. She hung herself upside down from a peg on the wall and pretended to be dead. An old, wise mouse peeked out, saw the cat, and said, 'You may look like you are dead, but I know your tricks. Even if you were stuffed with straw, I still wouldn't come near you.'
prerak_kahani.moral: The wise do not easily fall for the tricks of those who have deceived them in the past.

word_of_the_day.meaning: The action of deceiving someone; hiding the truth.
word_of_the_day.example: The magician's entire act relied on visual deception and quick hands.

did_you_know.fact: Did you know? Snails have thousands of tiny teeth located on a ribbon-like structure called a radula.

prerak_kahani.title: The Astronomer
prerak_kahani.story: An astronomer used to go out every night to look at the stars. One night, as he wandered through the fields with his eyes fixed on the sky, he didn't notice the path ahead and fell into a deep, dry well. As he cried out for help, a passerby heard him, looked down into the well, and said, 'You were so busy looking at the heavens that you forgot to look at what was right in front of your feet.'
prerak_kahani.moral: While it is good to have high goals and dreams, do not lose sight of practical reality.

word_of_the_day.meaning: Of or concerned with the actual doing or use of something rather than with theory and ideas.
word_of_the_day.example: He has a lot of big ideas, but he needs to figure out a practical way to execute them.

prerak_kahani.title: The Stag at the Pool
prerak_kahani.story: A thirsty stag went to a pool to drink water. Looking at his reflection, he felt incredibly proud of his large, magnificent antlers. But when he looked at his thin, spindly legs, he felt deeply ashamed of them. Suddenly, a lion appeared and chased him. His thin, strong legs helped him run incredibly fast, but when he entered the forest, his large, magnificent antlers got tangled in the branches, allowing the lion to catch him.
prerak_kahani.moral: What is most valuable is often what we despise the most, and what we admire can sometimes lead to our downfall.

word_of_the_day.meaning: Existing or occurring at or on the surface; not thorough, deep, or complete.
word_of_the_day.example: He only cared about superficial things like looks and money, rather than kindness.

prerak_kahani.title: The Old Man and Death
prerak_kahani.story: An exhausted old man carrying a heavy load of wood dropped his bundle and cried out, 'Life is too hard! I wish Death would just come and take me!' Immediately, the Grim Reaper appeared and asked, 'You called for me? What do you want?' Terrified, the old man quickly replied, 'Oh, I just needed some help lifting this heavy bundle of wood back onto my shoulders!'
prerak_kahani.moral: People often complain about their lives and ask for things they do not truly want when faced with reality.

word_of_the_day.meaning: The acceptance of something undesirable but inevitable.
word_of_the_day.example: He sighed with resignation as he realized he had missed the last train home.

prerak_kahani.title: The Wolf and the Shepherds
prerak_kahani.story: A wolf, unable to catch any sheep because of the fierce guard dogs, decided to sneak up and see how the shepherds lived. He crept close to their tent and peered inside. To his surprise, he saw the shepherds sitting around a fire, happily eating a feast of roasted mutton. The wolf muttered to himself, 'If I did that, they would hunt me down, but they do it themselves and no one says a word!'
prerak_kahani.moral: Men often condemn in others the very things they practice themselves.

word_of_the_day.meaning: A rule or principle which is unfairly applied in different ways to different people or groups.
word_of_the_day.example: It is a double standard to expect employees to arrive on time when the boss is always late.

today_in_history.fact: On November 22, 1995, Pixar's 'Toy Story,' the first entirely computer-animated feature film, was released in theaters.

did_you_know.fact: Did you know? Butterflies taste their food with their feet, which possess taste receptors to help them find nectar.

quote_of_the_day.quote: He who is without sin among you, let him be the first to throw a stone.
quote_of_the_day.author: Jesus Christ

paheli.question: What is so delicate that saying its name breaks it?

dialogue: Son: Dad, can you write in the dark?
Dad: I think so. Why?
Son: Good, because I need you to sign my report card.

prerak_kahani.title: The Farmer and His Sons
prerak_kahani.story: A dying farmer wanted to ensure his idle sons would learn how to work the farm. He called them to his bedside and told them that a great treasure was buried somewhere in the vineyards. After he passed, the sons dug up every inch of the soil looking for the treasure. They found no gold, but because they had thoroughly turned and aerated the soil, the vineyard produced a massive, profitable crop.
prerak_kahani.moral: Hard work is a treasure in itself.

word_of_the_day.meaning: Diligent and hard-working.
word_of_the_day.example: The industrious team completed the project two weeks ahead of schedule.

today_in_history.fact: On November 23, 1924, Edwin Hubble's discovery that the Andromeda 'nebula' is actually another galaxy was published, changing our view of the universe.

did_you_know.fact: Did you know? The shortest war in history lasted only 38 to 45 minutes, between Britain and Zanzibar in 1896.

quote_of_the_day.quote: There are no secrets to success. It is the result of preparation, hard work, and learning from failure.
quote_of_the_day.author: Colin Powell

paheli.question: I can fill a room, but I take up no space. What am I?

dialogue: Customer: Waiter, there's a dead fly in my soup!
Waiter: Yes sir, it's the hot water that kills them.

prerak_kahani.title: The North Wind and the Sun
prerak_kahani.story: The North Wind and the Sun argued over who was stronger. They saw a traveler and agreed that whoever could make the man take his coat off would be the winner. The Wind blew fiercely, but the colder it got, the tighter the man wrapped his coat around himself. Then, the Sun shined warmly and gently. As it got hotter, the traveler cheerfully took his coat off.
prerak_kahani.moral: Persuasion and gentleness are often more effective than force and aggression.

word_of_the_day.meaning: The act of convincing someone to do or believe something through reasoning or argument.
word_of_the_day.example: Through gentle persuasion, she convinced him to finally visit the doctor.

today_in_history.fact: On November 24, 1859, British naturalist Charles Darwin published his groundbreaking book 'On the Origin of Species'.

did_you_know.fact: Did you know? A shrimp's heart is located inside its head.

quote_of_the_day.quote: Force is all-conquering, but its victories are short-lived.
quote_of_the_day.author: Abraham Lincoln

paheli.question: The more you take, the more you leave behind. What are they?

dialogue: Patient: Doctor, I think I'm a moth!
Doctor: You need a psychiatrist, not a physician. Why did you come here?
Patient: Because the light was on!

prerak_kahani.title: The Fox and the Mask
prerak_kahani.story: A fox crept into an actor's house and rummaged through his belongings. He found a beautifully carved and painted mask used in plays. The fox put his paw on it, turned it over, and admired the craftsmanship. After looking at it for a while, he sighed and said, 'What a beautiful, handsome head! It is a great pity that it has absolutely no brains inside it.'
prerak_kahani.moral: Physical beauty is of little value if there is no intelligence or substance behind it.

word_of_the_day.meaning: The real physical matter of which a person or thing consists; solid basis or reality.
word_of_the_day.example: The politician's speech sounded great, but it lacked any real substance.

today_in_history.fact: On November 25, 1915, Albert Einstein presented his theory of general relativity to the Prussian Academy of Sciences.

did_you_know.fact: Did you know? Venus is the only planet in our solar system that spins clockwise; all the others spin counter-clockwise.

quote_of_the_day.quote: It is not the face, but the expressions on it. It is not the voice, but what you say. It is not how you look in that body, but the thing you do with it.
quote_of_the_day.author: Unknown

paheli.question: What is bought by the yard but worn by the foot?

dialogue: Friend 1: My dog used to chase people on a bike a lot.
Friend 2: Really? How did you stop him?
Friend 1: I finally took his bike away!

prerak_kahani.title: The Bear and the Travelers
prerak_kahani.story: Two travelers were walking in the woods when a bear suddenly appeared. One traveler quickly climbed a tall tree and hid. The other, knowing he couldn't outrun the bear, threw himself on the ground and held his breath, pretending to be dead. The bear sniffed him, whispered in his ear, and walked away. The friend in the tree came down and asked, 'What did the bear whisper?' The man replied, 'He told me never to travel with a friend who deserts you at the first sign of danger.'
prerak_kahani.moral: Misfortune tests the sincerity of friends.

word_of_the_day.meaning: Consistently good in quality or performance; able to be trusted.
word_of_the_day.example: He is a very reliable friend; you can always count on him in an emergency.

today_in_history.fact: November 26 is celebrated as Constitution Day in India, marking the adoption of the Indian Constitution in 1949.

did_you_know.fact: Did you know? Humans are the only animals in the world known to blush.

quote_of_the_day.quote: A true friend is one who walks in when the rest of the world walks out.
quote_of_the_day.author: Walter Winchell

paheli.question: What gets sharper the more you use it, but dulls if left alone?

dialogue: Employee: Can I have a few days off? I'm getting married.
Boss: Sure, but remember, marriage is an institution in which a man loses his Bachelor's degree and the woman gets her Master's!

prerak_kahani.title: The Crow and the Pitcher
prerak_kahani.story: A crow, half-dead with thirst, came upon a pitcher that had once been full of water. When the crow put its beak into the mouth of the pitcher, he found that only very little water was left in it, and he could not reach far enough down to get at it. Instead of giving up, the crow took a pebble and dropped it into the pitcher. He kept dropping pebbles one by one until the water rose to the brim, and he could drink.
prerak_kahani.moral: Little by little does the trick. Necessity is the mother of invention.

word_of_the_day.meaning: The quality of being clever, original, and inventive.
word_of_the_day.example: The stranded astronauts used sheer ingenuity to repair their broken ship.

today_in_history.fact: On November 27, 1895, Alfred Nobel signed his last will, establishing the Nobel Prizes.

did_you_know.fact: Did you know? Honey is the only food made by insects that humans can eat, and it never spoils.

quote_of_the_day.quote: Where there is a will, there is a way.
quote_of_the_day.author: English Proverb

paheli.question: What building has the most stories?

dialogue: Teacher: Tell me a sentence that starts with an 'I'.
Student: I is the...
Teacher: Stop! Always say 'I am'.
Student: Alright, I am the ninth letter of the alphabet.

prerak_kahani.title: The Lion and the Mouse
prerak_kahani.story: A sleeping lion was awakened by a mouse running across his nose. The lion woke up angry and caught the mouse, intending to eat it. The mouse pleaded for his life, promising to return the favor one day. The lion laughed at the idea but let him go. Weeks later, the lion was caught in a hunter's net and roared in frustration. The little mouse heard him, ran over, and gnawed through the ropes, freeing the mighty beast.
prerak_kahani.moral: No act of kindness, no matter how small, is ever wasted.

word_of_the_day.meaning: Sympathetic pity and concern for the sufferings or misfortunes of others.
word_of_the_day.example: He showed great compassion by donating most of his wealth to charity.

today_in_history.fact: On November 28, 1520, Ferdinand Magellan entered the Pacific Ocean, becoming the first European explorer to reach it via the Atlantic.

did_you_know.fact: Did you know? The hashtag symbol (#) is technically called an octothorpe.

quote_of_the_day.quote: Kindness is a language which the deaf can hear and the blind can see.
quote_of_the_day.author: Mark Twain

paheli.question: What is full of holes but still holds water?

dialogue: Man: I'm terrified of elevators.
Woman: Oh, I'm sure you'll get over it.
Man: I don't know, I've started taking steps to avoid them.

prerak_kahani.title: The Gnat and the Bull
prerak_kahani.story: A tiny gnat flew over a meadow and settled on the tip of one of the horns of a massive bull. After resting for a while, the gnat prepared to fly away. But before leaving, he buzzed in the bull's ear, 'Excuse me, I hope I wasn't too heavy for you. I will leave now so your neck doesn't ache.' The bull replied lazily, 'I didn't even know you were there, and I certainly won't notice when you leave.'
prerak_kahani.moral: We are often less important in the eyes of others than we think we are.

word_of_the_day.meaning: Too small or unimportant to be worth consideration.
word_of_the_day.example: Compared to the size of the universe, our planet is incredibly insignificant.

today_in_history.fact: On November 29, 1972, the first commercially successful video game, Pong, was released by Atari.

did_you_know.fact: Did you know? Peanuts are not nuts at all; they are legumes, like peas and lentils.

quote_of_the_day.quote: Ego is the anesthesia that deadens the pain of stupidity.
quote_of_the_day.author: Frank Leahy

paheli.question: I have an eye but cannot see. I am faster than any man, yet I have no limbs. What am I?

dialogue: Kid 1: What do you call a fake noodle?
Kid 2: I have no idea.
Kid 1: An impasta!

prerak_kahani.title: The Woodcutter and the Axe
prerak_kahani.story: A young, strong woodcutter asked for a job at a timber merchant's site and got it. The first day he chopped down 18 trees. The next day, he worked even harder but only brought down 15 trees. The third day, despite trying his best, he only chopped 10. The boss came over and asked, 'When was the last time you sharpened your axe?' The woodcutter replied, 'I had no time to sharpen my axe; I have been too busy cutting trees.'
prerak_kahani.moral: Working hard is not enough; you must also take time to improve your skills and tools.

word_of_the_day.meaning: The action or process of making ready or being made ready for use or consideration.
word_of_the_day.example: Thorough preparation is the key to a successful performance.

today_in_history.fact: On November 30, 1982, Michael Jackson's 'Thriller,' the best-selling album of all time, was released.

did_you_know.fact: Did you know? Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood.

quote_of_the_day.quote: Give me six hours to chop down a tree and I will spend the first four sharpening the axe.
quote_of_the_day.author: Abraham Lincoln
